Original Review Text:
They are great if they ever show up. Taskrabbit has become a bait-and-switch machine with a calendar attached.

I tried to use the platform for same-day organization help and ended up wasting more time managing Taskers than the task itself. The pattern is exhausting: people accept or engage with the job, ask endless pre-task questions, request photos, change the terms, suggest extra people or extra costs, delay arrival, and then flake or become impossible to pin down.

This was not a complicated mystery project. I needed hands-on organization help: show up, assess in person, sort, move, bag, organize, and make progress. Instead, I got treated like I was applying for permission to hire someone.

The worst part is that this is not a one-off. Out of the last 15 Taskers I have tried to hire, 13 have flaked in some form. That is not bad luck. That is a platform reliability problem.

When people are charging $40 to $80 an hour, I expect basic professionalism: clear communication, a real ETA, no last-minute changes to the deal, and the ability to actually show up. If a Tasker needs to inspect photos, renegotiate the job, bring another person, or decide whether the task is “worth it,” that should happen before they present themselves as available.

Taskrabbit markets itself as a way to get help quickly. In practice, it has become a second job: screening, messaging, following up, documenting, canceling, and starting over. The platform may have useful people somewhere in the haystack, but the experience of finding them has become ridiculous.

I canceled because it was no longer worth my time. The task was supposed to reduce chaos, not create a new administrative circus.

Disappointed. Hello Thumbtack Support,

I wanted to share my frustration regarding the growing number of issues with the app. I’ve been patient for a long time, but lately it’s becoming increasingly difficult to work with your platform.

The biggest question I have is: why were customer phone numbers hidden? This has made communication much more difficult. While some clients don’t mind using the in-app messenger, many prefer regular text messaging. Hiding phone numbers has created a significant problem for professionals trying to provide fast service.

* New messages often do not move to the top of the conversation list. Instead, they remain buried where the chat originally started, making it easy to miss important customer messages.
* Unread message notifications remain visible long after messages have already been read.
* Lead notifications continue showing for several minutes even after the lead has already been opened and reviewed.
* Every time I open the app, I’m repeatedly asked to upgrade to Platinum, even though I have already been a Platinum Pro for months. Why am I constantly seeing these prompts?
* There have also been situations where I felt I was charged twice for what appeared to be the same opportunity.

On top of these issues, lead prices continue to increase while lead quality and matching seem to be getting worse. It feels like I’m paying more while receiving less value.

I have invested several thousand dollars into Thumbtack over the years because I believed in the platform and relied on it for my business. However, the app experience has noticeably declined, and it is becoming difficult to justify continuing to invest in it.

Thankfully, there are other platforms available, and I have built strong reputations and reviews elsewhere as well. That said, I am disappointed because I expected Thumbtack to remain one of my primary sources of business.

Can you please explain:

1. Why customer phone numbers were hidden?
2. Whether there are plans to restore direct phone access?

Victor

Injustice. I have been using Thumbtack for about two and a half years, and during that time I’ve spent thousands of dollars on leads. So I believe I have enough experience to give honest feedback about the platform.

Unfortunately, over the past couple of years it feels like the company has focused more on improving its system for charging professionals rather than improving the quality of the platform itself.

The main issue is that professionals are paying for leads that often have very low intent or no response at all. Many clients don’t answer calls, don’t understand the scope of work, or never planned to hire anyone in the first place. Yet professionals still pay for those leads.

Another problem is that clients are not educated about the platform. There is no real accountability for them. Clients can request multiple professionals, ignore everyone, cancel, or even leave unfair reviews without understanding the work involved. Meanwhile professionals carry all the financial risk.

Professionals are the ones bringing revenue to this platform, yet we have very little protection. Clients can threaten bad reviews, ask for discounts after the work is done, or refuse to pay. When a complaint happens, the professional’s account can be suspended quickly, which can instantly affect someone’s livelihood.

Over the past two years I’ve also noticed lead prices increasing, but the quality of leads has not improved.

Many professionals I speak with say the same thing:
we are willing to pay for real leads and real customers, but paying for unresponsive or unqualified leads simply doesn’t feel fair.

Thumbtack could be an incredible platform if it focused more on balance between customers and professionals. A system where professionals only pay for real connections or confirmed projects would be much more sustainable.

Right now it often feels like the platform benefits from volume, while the professionals carry most of the risk.

I hope Thumbtack listens to the professionals who actually power this marketplace and works on improving the system for everyone.

Unfair app. This is what happened to me twice:
And they never refund me. The scheme is easy as pie:

The request from a Thumbtack client for a cleaner to pay movers is a known scam, specifically a variation of the "overpayment" or "fake check" scam. The "hack" for a professional is to recognize this red flag and cease communication immediately. 
Here is how the scam typically works and why you should be wary:
The Scenario: A "client" (scammer) will contact you for a cleaning job and mention that they are out of state or otherwise unavailable. They will often offer to pay a generous amount, sometimes more than your quote, and say they will send you a check for both the cleaning and the movers.
The Request: They will ask you to pay the movers (who are actually the scammer or an accomplice) with the extra money from the check.
The Trap (Fake Check): The check they send you is fake, but it may initially appear to clear in your bank account due to banking laws that require funds to be made available quickly.
The Loss: You will then wire the money to the "movers". A few days or weeks later, your bank will realize the check is fraudulent and reverse the deposit, and you will be responsible for the money you sent to the scammer. 
What to Do:
Do NOT pay anyone else on their behalf. Your service is cleaning, not logistics or payments for other services.
Do NOT accept checks, especially for amounts higher than your service fee, and never agree to wire money. Stick to secure payment methods that you can verify and trust, ideally through the Thumbtack platform or direct, secure electronic payments.
